extra.explanation: China is exporting its way through weak domestic demand, with a nine-month trade surplus near $938 billion. That means cheaper Chinese EVs, steel and solar in other markets, and more tariffs in response.
options: More price pressure from cheap Chinese goods, and more trade friction
Less competition as China focuses on its home market
Higher Chinese demand for their finished goods
A much stronger yuan that makes Chinese goods expensive
extra.prompt: China's September exports jumped about 36%. What is the most likely effect on manufacturers in other countries?

extra.explanation: Higher inflation keeps the Fed from cutting and pushes long-term yields up. With 30-year mortgages near 7.4%, builder confidence fell to its lowest since 2012 and 43% of builders cut prices.
options: Builders use oil as their main raw material
It pushes home prices up too fast for buyers
It keeps interest rates, and so mortgage rates, high, which freezes demand
Gasoline taxes are added to home prices
extra.prompt: Why does oil-driven inflation hurt US homebuilders?

extra.explanation: Contract rates are fixed for the year, while diesel rose about 68% since before the Iran war. Surcharges recover part of that cost, but late, so carriers are cutting maintenance and delaying new trucks.
options: Freight volumes fell to almost nothing
Their rates were set before fuel rose, and fuel surcharges only pass costs on with a lag
Regulators capped trucking rates
Driver wages fell sharply
extra.prompt: Truckers on fixed annual contracts are losing money with diesel near $6.30. Why?

extra.explanation: With revenue down 15% and paying users down 16%, Bumble needs time to rework its product. Private ownership lets it experiment without reporting to public investors every quarter.
options: To raise cheaper equity from the public
Regulators required it
To pay a large special dividend to public shareholders
To restructure and rebuild the product without quarterly public-market pressure
extra.prompt: Bumble is going private at $1.3B, down from roughly $14B at its IPO. What is the usual main reason a board chooses a take-private in this situation?

extra.explanation: Drug sales grew about 8% and outpaced devices. Separating slower units, as J&J did with Kenvue in 2023, lets each business be valued and run on its own terms.
options: Focus capital and management on higher-margin, faster-growing businesses like drugs
Avoid a patent cliff in orthopedics
Merge orthopedics into Kenvue
Exit healthcare altogether
extra.prompt: J&J is leaning toward spinning off its orthopedics unit. What is the main strategic logic?

questions.explanation: Hormuz tanker transits are running about 70% below pre-war levels. The oil exists but can't move safely, so freight, insurance and the physical premium drive the price. OPEC+ doesn't meet until Nov 1.
options: OPEC+ announced a large production cut
Attacks on shipping mean Gulf oil can't safely get through the Strait of Hormuz
US shale output fell sharply this quarter
Chinese oil demand surged on a strong recovery
questions.prompt: Brent is near $110 even though the world's oil reserves haven't changed. What is the main reason?

questions.explanation: An exporter buys gas near $3, liquefies and ships it, and sells near $29. That spread is the margin. European and Asian buyers pay the high price, and US households just see normal domestic prices.
options: European factories that use gas
Japanese utilities buying cargoes on the spot market
US LNG exporters with cargoes to sell
US households heating with gas
questions.prompt: US gas (Henry Hub) is about $3/MMBtu while Asian spot LNG is about $29. Who captures the most value from that gap?

questions.explanation: CoreWeave rents GPUs under contracts concentrated in a few customers and funded its fleet largely with debt. If those customers spend less, revenue and debt service are both at risk, which is why it fell 25%+ in last week's sell-off.
options: A debt-funded AI cloud provider with a few very large customers, like CoreWeave
A payment network like Visa
A consumer staples company like Procter & Gamble
A large US bank
questions.prompt: Which kind of company is most exposed if big tech firms cut their AI data center spending?

questions.explanation: Proofpoint sells email security and Varonis sells data security, both to corporate security chiefs. The logic is revenue synergy: sell both products to each customer. This 'platform plus add-on' approach is a classic private equity playbook.
options: Vertical integration into a supplier
A merger of two direct competitors to cut costs
Diversification into an unrelated industry
A platform company buying an adjacent product to cross-sell to the same buyers
questions.prompt: Thoma Bravo's Proofpoint is buying Varonis for $6.3B. How would you best describe the strategy?

questions.explanation: Regulators said the bank left more than $5 billion of suspicious activity unreported or reported late. The OCC's $750 million share was the largest civil penalty in its history. American Express was fined $350 million for similar failures a week earlier.
options: It failed to properly monitor and report suspicious transactions under anti-money-laundering rules
It held too little capital against its loans
It misled investors about interest rate risk
It broke consumer rules on overdraft fees
questions.prompt: Why was Bank of America hit with more than $1.2 billion in penalties?

questions.explanation: Management pointed to low imports and long lead times under the current trade environment. The flip side: automakers and other steel buyers pay more for their inputs.
options: Chinese demand for US steel surged
Iron ore became much cheaper
Trade protection keeps imports low, giving US mills pricing power
It merged with Nucor and cut capacity
questions.prompt: Cleveland-Cliffs' average steel price is up about 14% from a year ago. What is the main reason?

questions.explanation: Banks borrow cheaply through deposits and lend at higher rates. That spread, net interest income, is the largest profit line for most big banks. Fee businesses add steadier but smaller revenue.
options: Investment banking advisory fees
Net interest income: the spread between what it earns on loans and pays on deposits
Trading revenue
Late fees on credit cards
questions.prompt: For a large US bank, what is usually the single biggest source of profit?

questions.explanation: A patented drug earns very high margins until its patent expires, then sales drop sharply as generics or biosimilars arrive. Buying biotechs refills the pipeline. J&J said this week that new drug deals will weigh on its 2027 earnings.
options: To lower their manufacturing costs
To move into medical devices
To replace revenue they'll lose when patents on their blockbuster drugs expire
To reduce the taxes they pay on research
questions.prompt: Why do big pharma companies keep buying biotech companies?

questions.explanation: Lenders fund LNG projects because buyers commit to long-term contracts up front, often priced at Henry Hub times 115% plus a fixed fee. The contracts make the cash flow predictable enough to borrow against.
options: By selling cargoes on the spot market as they are produced
Mostly through government grants
Through retail bonds sold to consumers
Against long-term, roughly 20-year, offtake contracts signed before construction
questions.prompt: How is a new $10B+ LNG export terminal typically financed?

questions.explanation: New US shale wells typically need around $60 to $65 a barrel. With WTI above $100, shale producers are very profitable, but they are prioritizing dividends and buybacks over fast growth.
options: About $20 a barrel
About $60 to $65 a barrel
About $110 a barrel
About $150 a barrel
questions.prompt: Roughly what oil price do new US shale wells need to break even?

extra.explanation: RTX reported $176B of commercial and $164B of defense backlog, about half each. That is more than three years of sales, so the constraint is output, not demand.
options: Almost all defense
About half commercial, half defense
Almost all commercial
Mostly space programs
extra.prompt: RTX's backlog reached $340 billion. Roughly how is it split?

extra.explanation: Passive funds must own what is in the index, so a downgrade turns into forced selling. Jakarta's index fell 11% on Friday and another 3.6% on Monday, after $4.9B of foreign outflows this year.
options: MSCI would ban foreign investors from buying Indonesian shares
Index funds would have to sell, raising Indonesian firms' cost of capital
Indonesian companies would have to stop paying dividends
The government would be forced to devalue the rupiah
extra.prompt: MSCI proposed moving Indonesia out of its Emerging Markets index. Why does that hurt Indonesian companies even if their businesses are unchanged?

extra.explanation: PBMs earn much of their money from a share of rebates and price spreads; flat fees cut that link. The three biggest PBMs (Optum Rx, Caremark, Express Scripts) are owned by UnitedHealth, CVS and Cigna.
options: Hospital chains such as HCA
Generic drug makers
Insurers that own big PBMs, such as UnitedHealth, CVS and Cigna
Medical device makers
extra.prompt: CMS proposed that PBMs in Medicare Part D be paid only flat service fees. Which companies are most exposed?

extra.explanation: Direct-to-device satellite service could erode carriers' coverage advantage. The four would own the spectrum and build ground networks, while a satellite partner (not yet chosen) supplies the constellation.
options: To keep satellite players as suppliers instead of direct competitors for coverage
To launch their own satellite constellation and stop using towers
Because EU rules require all operators to merge their networks
To sell the spectrum to SpaceX at a profit
extra.prompt: Why are Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefonica and Vodafone exploring a joint bid for satellite-to-phone spectrum?

extra.explanation: Silence's lead drug divesiran has strong Phase 2 data, and Merck's scale and commercial reach can speed it into Phase 3. A mid-stage biotech usually can't fund late trials and launch cheaply, so a sale captures value now.
options: Its drug has already been approved and launched
Regulators require biotechs to partner with big pharma
Big pharma pays for drugs only after patents expire
Funding Phase 3 trials and a global launch alone is very costly
extra.prompt: Merck KGaA is paying about $1.3B for Silence Therapeutics, whose shares jumped about 126%. Why does a small biotech often sell at this stage?

questions.explanation: Kpler shows Hormuz crude flows fell to about 8.5M b/d last week from over 20M the week before. The oil exists but can't be shipped safely, so freeing up Russian supply on paper barely changes the physical shortage.
options: OPEC+ cut output at the same time to offset Russian barrels
Russian oil exports were already banned worldwide by the EU
The shortage is physical: Gulf oil can't move safely through Hormuz
US shale producers announced large production cuts the same day
questions.prompt: President Trump waived the new tariffs on buyers of Russian energy, yet Brent stayed near $110. Why did the waiver do so little?

questions.explanation: Microsoft's NiSource deal uses a large-load rate class where big users fund the capacity they need, protecting existing customers. Connection timing is the other make-or-break issue: Microsoft just walked away from a UK site where grid power might not arrive until the 2030s.
options: Whether a large-load tariff makes the data center fund the new generation and grid, and how fast a firm connection can be delivered
Whether the utility can raise residential rates enough to pay for the new plants
Whether the data center will buy rooftop solar for its own buildings
Whether the utility's stock price would rise on the announcement
questions.prompt: A US utility is asked to supply a new 1 GW data center campus. What matters most to get right first?

questions.explanation: GM approved a new $20B multi-year buyback after completing a $6B program announced in January. The $6B figure is tempting but is the old program; GM's share count is down about 6% this year.
options: $2 billion
$6 billion
$10 billion
$20 billion
questions.prompt: How large is the new share buyback GM approved alongside its Q3 results?

questions.explanation: Engine makers often sell new engines at thin margins and earn most profit over decades of aftermarket service. With airlines flying older planes longer, services grew 17% and GE raised its 2026 EPS guide to $8.00-8.10.
options: Selling new engines at high margins to Boeing and Airbus
Spare parts, repairs and service on the engines already flying
Leasing aircraft to airlines
Government research grants for new engine designs
questions.prompt: GE Aerospace's orders jumped 49% while LEAP engine deliveries rose only 5%. Where does an engine maker like GE earn most of its profit?

questions.explanation: Metal cans are a mature, low-growth market, so the value comes from combining plants, purchasing and logistics. If the $225M of synergies arrive, the effective price falls from 7.1x to 4.8x EBITDA; if they don't, Silgan paid a full price.
options: The deal only works if Trivium grows sales quickly
Silgan is paying a high premium for a fast-growing business
Most of the value depends on delivering cost synergies in a mature industry
Private equity partner AIP is taking all the integration risk
questions.prompt: Trivium is priced at 7.1x EBITDA, but only 4.8x after $225M of expected synergies. What does that gap tell you about the Silgan deal?

questions.explanation: Gasoline was up 27.8% and energy 19%, while CPI-median (1.9%) and CPI-trim (1.8%) stayed near target. That is an oil shock, not broad inflation, though markets still price a December hike in case it spreads. Food was actually one of the softer items.
options: Price rises are driven by energy and haven't yet spread across the economy
Wages are rising fast and pushing up all prices
The Bank of Canada has kept interest rates too low for years
Food prices are the main driver of inflation
questions.prompt: Canada's headline inflation rose to 3.1%, but core measures were 1.8-1.9%. What does that combination mainly signal?

questions.explanation: US national health expenditure is about $4.9T, or 17-18% of GDP (CMS, 2023). About $10T is the rough global figure, not the US one.
options: About $1.5 trillion, roughly 5% of GDP
About $4.9 trillion, roughly 17-18% of GDP
About $10 trillion, roughly 35% of GDP
About $900 billion, roughly 3% of GDP
questions.prompt: Roughly how much does the US spend on healthcare each year?

extra.explanation: Intuitive earns most of its money after installation from instruments and service used in every procedure. It placed 546 da Vinci systems versus 427 a year earlier, which should lift procedures in coming quarters.
options: Robots are given away free, so procedures are the only sales
Procedures determine demand for instruments, accessories and service, which is its main recurring revenue
Procedure counts set the price of each robot
Procedures are the only thing regulators measure
extra.prompt: Why does Intuitive Surgical watch procedure growth (up 15%) more closely than robot sales alone?

extra.explanation: Europe has to bid for LNG when storage is low and Qatar capacity is partly offline, which helps exporters that can ship gas. Energy-intensive industry in Europe loses from higher gas prices.
options: European fertilizer makers that use gas as a raw material
US LNG exporters selling cargoes to Europe at higher prices
European households with fixed price contracts
Airlines that use gas for fuel
extra.prompt: Europe's gas storage was 68.5% full on Sept 15 versus 80.6% a year earlier. Who is most likely to gain?

extra.explanation: Hiring is weak but inflation is far above the 2% goal, so neither a cut nor a quick hike is clearly right. Markets leaned toward a hold on October 28 and a possible hike in December.
options: Weak hiring argues for waiting while energy-driven inflation argues against cutting
Inflation is below target, so cutting is easy
Unemployment fell sharply, so hiring is strong
The Fed does not consider jobs data
extra.prompt: The Fed's rate is 3.75-4.00% and inflation is 3.4%, but September payrolls grew only 29,000. Why is the Fed's choice hard?

extra.explanation: Japanese insurers face a shrinking home market and are buying overseas retirement businesses. Dai-ichi already holds 20.36% and offered A$11.80 a share, although the bid is non-binding.
options: Japan has no demand for retirement income
Annuities need no investment portfolio
Australia's ageing population creates steady demand for guaranteed retirement income, offsetting a shrinking Japanese market
Annuities are exempt from regulation
extra.prompt: Why does Challenger's annuity business appeal to a Japanese life insurer?

extra.explanation: Content is expensive to make but cheap to deliver, so more subscribers, price rises and ads improve margins. Netflix's 34.6% operating margin shows what scale does.
options: Selling movie tickets
Spreading a large fixed content budget over more subscribers and higher prices and ad income
Charging for each hour viewed
Selling its original shows to cable networks
extra.prompt: What is the main way a streaming service makes a profit?

questions.explanation: The AI business (Super Intelligence) earned $7.6B against about $5.2B for connectivity, so SpaceX now gets more than half its revenue from AI computing. The tempting answer, Starlink, is still growing 69% but is now the smaller segment.
options: Starlink subscriptions still provide most of its revenue
Rocket launches now bring in the largest share of sales
AI computing revenue of $7.6B passed Starlink's roughly $5.2B for the first time
Government contracts replaced consumer sales as the main driver
questions.prompt: SpaceX's Q3 revenue was $14.6B, up 161%. Which statement best describes what changed about the business?

questions.explanation: Sites that are slow and hard to approve create barriers to entry, and multi-year contracts make cash flow predictable enough to carry debt. Cleanaway has 300+ sites and EQT is paying A$3.095 a share, 32.1% over the pre-approach price.
options: Landfills and treatment sites are hard to permit and replicate, and contracts give steady cash flow it can finance with debt
Waste volumes double when the economy slows, so profits rise in recessions
Waste companies need little investment, so almost all profit can be paid out
Governments guarantee waste companies a minimum share price
questions.prompt: Why would an infrastructure fund pay a 32% premium to take a waste company like Cleanaway private?

questions.explanation: Service firms are paid for wells drilled and completed, so revenue follows producers' activity plans rather than the spot price. Halliburton's $2.2B North America figure and weaker pressure pumping show spending restraint, while international work grew.
options: Oilfield service firms are paid based on the oil price in each barrel produced
US producers are not adding drilling and completion work in proportion to the price rise, and service demand follows that activity
Halliburton stopped working in North America
Higher oil prices always reduce drilling activity immediately
questions.prompt: Brent is near $110, yet Halliburton's North America revenue fell 5% from the prior quarter. What is the most likely explanation?

questions.explanation: Industrial output grew 5.5% while retail sales and investment lagged, so the headline number rests on factories and exports. That matters for exporters of steel and other commodities, which feel the property drop most, and invites trade friction.
options: Domestic consumers are driving the expansion
The property sector is now a major growth engine
Growth is balanced across consumption, investment and exports
Growth is leaning on exports and industry while households and property stay weak
questions.prompt: China grew 4.5% in Q3, but retail sales rose just 1.1% and property investment fell 20.6%. What does this combination suggest?

questions.explanation: A book-to-bill above 1 means new contracts exceed revenue recognized, so the order book grows. The $110B record backlog is a multi-year pipeline, though cost overruns on fixed-price programs remain the main risk.
options: Sales will fall because customers are cancelling orders
Revenue growth must be coming from price cuts
Orders are outrunning sales, so the backlog (about $110B) is growing and supports future revenue
The company is selling more than it can deliver this year
questions.prompt: Northrop Grumman won $16B of net awards on $11.1B of sales, a book-to-bill of 1.5. What does that tell you?

questions.explanation: Netflix said Q3 benefited mainly from the timing of expenses, and Q4 carries about 120 basis points of drag from the roughly 1,000-person cut. Revenue is still growing about 12%, so the drop is about cost timing, not demand.
options: Expense timing helped Q3, and Q4 includes about 1.2 points of cost from the job cuts
Subscribers fell sharply in the fall
The company plans to cut prices to attract new viewers
Advertising revenue is expected to decline
questions.prompt: Netflix earned a 34.6% operating margin in Q3 but guided to 26.0% for Q4. What best explains the drop?

questions.explanation: Planes, crews and airports cost about the same whether seats are full or not, so profit is a thin slice of revenue. With IATA now forecasting a 2.0% margin and jet fuel at about $152 a barrel, fuel swings dominate.
options: Airlines hold no fixed assets, so costs vary with each flight
Net margins are only about 2-4% and most other costs are fixed, so small cost moves are a large share of profit
Fuel is the only cost airlines pay
Fuel contracts are always fixed for ten years
questions.prompt: Why can a small rise in fuel costs wipe out most of an airline's profit?
